speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe in detail when your right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and falls began, and whether these symptoms have been getting worse over time. Additionally, can you clarify which specific memories you have been forgetting and give me examples of the paranoid thoughts you are experiencing?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Subacute Combined Degeneration of the spinal cord due to Vitamin B12 deficiency. The combination of acute motor weakness, gait ataxia, and subacute cognitive/psychiatric changes (forgetfulness, paranoia) in a 44-year-old male is highly characteristic of this condition, which can present with psychiatric symptoms before significant neurological deficits become apparent.
